Absolutely! Here’s a **comprehensive 12-week summary** for your client, integrating strength, cardio, mobility, nutrition, and fun elements. This is designed for a beginner in a small flat with a yoga mat and pull-up bar, and includes all the upgrades you requested.

---

# **12-Week Home Strength & Fitness Plan: Summary**

---

## **Programme Structure**

- **Strength Training:** 3x/week (Mon/Wed/Fri)
- **Cardio:** 2–3x/week (Tue/Thu/Sat)
- **Finisher Day:** Saturday (fun, challenging circuit)
- **Mobility:** 3–5x/week (as warm-up, cool-down, or on rest days)
- **Nutrition:** High-protein, whole-foods-based, with sample meal structure

---

## **Phases**

| Phase         | Weeks | Focus                        |
|---------------|-------|-----------------------------|
| Foundation    | 1–4   | Technique, base strength, aerobic base, habits |
| Progression   | 5–8   | Increased intensity, harder variations, HIIT   |
| Peak/Consolidation | 9–11 | Advanced bodyweight, peak effort, conditioning |
| Deload/Test   | 12    | Recovery, assessment, goal setting             |

---

## **Weekly Template**

| Day        | Activity                        |
|------------|---------------------------------|
| Monday     | Strength + Mobility             |
| Tuesday    | Cardio + Mobility               |
| Wednesday  | Strength + Mobility             |
| Thursday   | Cardio or Rest + Mobility       |
| Friday     | Strength + Mobility             |
| Saturday   | Finisher Day (Fun Circuit/Cardio) + Mobility |
| Sunday     | Rest + Mobility                 |

---

## **Strength Training Progression**

### **Weeks 1–4: Foundation**
- **Exercises:** Incline push-ups, assisted pull-ups/negatives, bodyweight squats, glute bridges, planks, dead bugs, bird dogs
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 rounds, 8–15 reps, 60s rest
- **Focus:** Form, consistency, adding reps each week

### **Weeks 5–8: Progression (Intensity Up)**
- **Exercises:** Regular/decline/close-grip push-ups, pull-ups (negatives, isometrics, unassisted as able), Bulgarian split squats, single-leg glute bridges, pike push-ups, hollow holds
- **Sets/Reps:** 4–5 rounds, 8–15 reps, 45–60s rest, tempo/pauses, AMRAP finishers
- **Focus:** Harder variations, slower tempo, more sets, less rest

### **Weeks 9–11: Peak/Consolidation**
- **Exercises:** Decline/archer push-ups, unassisted pull-ups, pistol squats to chair, hip thrusts, hanging knee raises, advanced core
- **Sets/Reps:** 4–5 rounds, 8–12 reps, 45–75s rest, AMRAP last set
- **Focus:** Max intensity, advanced moves, peak effort

### **Week 12: Deload & Assessment**
- **Exercises:** Best variation of push-up, pull-up, squat, glute bridge, plank
- **Sets/Reps:** 2–3 rounds, AMRAP (max reps), max plank hold
- **Focus:** Test progress, active recovery, set new goals

---

## **Cardio Plan**

### **Weeks 1–4: Foundation**
- **2x/week, 20–25 min:** March/jog in place, step-ups, shadow boxing, high knees, circuit style

### **Weeks 5–8: Progression**
- **2–3x/week, 25–30 min:** HIIT circuits (jumping jacks, mountain climbers, squat jumps, shadow boxing), Tabata, or brisk walking in place

### **Weeks 9–12: Peak**
- **3x/week, 25–30 min:** Mixed HIIT & LISS, more rounds, higher intensity, finishers (burpees, squat jumps, etc.)

---

## **Saturday Finisher Day (“Bodyweight Gauntlet”)**

- **Warm-up:** Dynamic moves (jumping jacks, inchworms, etc.)
- **Main Circuit:** 3–4 rounds, 40s work/20s rest per move (pull-up bar hang/pull-ups, push-up to Down Dog, lunges, mountain climbers, plank shoulder taps, squat jumps, shadow boxing)
- **Fun Finisher:** Rotating challenge (pull-up ladder, core countdown, deck of cards, Tabata blast)
- **Cool-down:** Full-body stretch

---

## **Mobility Routine (3–5x/week)**

- **Moves:** Cat-cow, World’s Greatest Stretch, Downward Dog to Cobra, 90/90 hip rotations, thoracic rotations, shoulder dislocates, deep squat hold, hip flexor stretch, child’s pose with side reach, neck circles
- **Duration:** 15–20 min/session

---

## **Nutrition Plan**

- **Calories:** Maintenance + 200–300 kcal for muscle gain (adjust as needed)
- **Protein:** 1.2–1.6g/kg bodyweight daily
- **Carbs:** 3–5g/kg
- **Fats:** 0.8–1g/kg
- **Meals:** 3 main meals + 1–2 snacks, protein at every meal, plenty of veg/fruit, whole grains, healthy fats
- **Hydration:** 2–3L water/day
- **Supplements (optional):** Whey/plant protein, creatine, multivitamin, vitamin D

---

## **Equipment Recommendations (for future progression)**

- **Adjustable dumbbells** (2–20kg+ per hand)
- **Resistance bands** (variety of strengths)
- **Kettlebell** (12–16kg to start)
- **Weighted vest** (up to 10–20kg)

---

## **Progression & Assessment**

- **Add reps, sets, or harder variations as able**
- **Track max reps for push-ups, pull-ups, squats, planks at start, week 6, and week 12**
- **Adjust nutrition and rest as needed for recovery and results**

---

## **Sample Week (e.g., Week 6)**

| Day        | Activity                                      |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Monday     | Strength (Progression circuit) + Mobility     |
| Tuesday    | Cardio (HIIT circuit) + Mobility              |
| Wednesday  | Strength (Progression circuit) + Mobility     |
| Thursday   | Cardio (Tabata or LISS) + Mobility            |
| Friday     | Strength (Progression circuit) + Mobility     |
| Saturday   | Finisher Day (Bodyweight Gauntlet) + Mobility |
| Sunday     | Rest + Mobility                               |

---

**This plan will build strength, muscle, fitness, and mobility, while keeping things fresh and fun.**

Absolutely! Here’s a comprehensive 12-week strength programme for your beginner client, designed for minimal equipment (yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar) and a small living space. The plan is progressive, focusing on foundational bodyweight strength, pull-up bar skills, and overall mobility. Each week includes three full-body sessions, with clear progression and deloading phases.

---

## **Programme Overview**

- **Duration:** 12 weeks
- **Frequency:** 3 sessions/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri)
- **Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar
- **Session Length:** 35–45 minutes
- **Focus:** Full-body strength, progressive overload, mobility, and core stability

---

## **Phases**

1. **Foundation (Weeks 1–4):** Learn movement patterns, build base strength, master technique.
2. **Progression (Weeks 5–8):** Increase intensity, introduce more challenging variations, volume.
3. **Consolidation & Peak (Weeks 9–11):** Push intensity, advanced variations, peak strength.
4. **Deload & Assessment (Week 12):** Reduce volume, test progress, focus on recovery.

---

## **Weekly Structure**

Each session includes:
- **Warm-up (5–7 min):** Mobility and activation
- **Main Strength Circuit (25–30 min):** 5–6 exercises, circuit or superset style
- **Core/Accessory (5–7 min):** Focused core or mobility work
- **Cool-down (3–5 min):** Stretching

---

# **Detailed 12-Week Plan**

---

## **Weeks 1–4: Foundation**

**Goals:** Learn form, build consistency, establish baseline strength.

**Warm-up (all sessions):**
- Cat-cow x10
- Downward dog to plank x8
- Arm circles x10/side
- Glute bridge x10
- Bodyweight squat x10

**Main Circuit (3 rounds, 60s rest between rounds):**

| Exercise                | Sets x Reps         | Notes                        |
|-------------------------|---------------------|------------------------------|
| Incline Push-up (hands on table/chair) | 3x8–12           | Focus on full range         |
| Doorway Pull-up (assisted, jump or slow negative) | 3x3–5            | Use chair for assistance    |
| Bodyweight Squat        | 3x12–15             | Slow, controlled             |
| Glute Bridge            | 3x12–15             | Squeeze at top               |
| Plank                   | 3x20–30 sec         | Maintain form                |

**Core/Accessory:**
- Dead bug x10/side
- Bird dog x10/side

**Cool-down:**
- Forward fold, quad stretch, chest opener

**Progression:** Add 1–2 reps per set each week if possible.

---

## **Weeks 5–8: Progression**

**Goals:** Increase intensity, introduce harder variations, more volume.

**Warm-up:** As above, add 30s jumping jacks.

**Main Circuit (4 rounds, 60s rest):**

| Exercise                | Sets x Reps         | Notes                        |
|-------------------------|---------------------|------------------------------|
| Push-up (regular or incline as needed) | 4x8–12           | Lower to floor, full range  |
| Pull-up (assisted, slow negative, or isometric hold at top) | 4x3–6            | Reduce assistance over time |
| Bulgarian Split Squat (rear foot on chair) | 4x8/leg          | Control, depth              |
| Single-leg Glute Bridge | 4x8/leg             | Pause at top                 |
| Hollow Body Hold        | 4x20–30 sec         | Lower back flat              |

**Core/Accessory:**
- Side plank x20s/side
- Superman x10

**Cool-down:** As above

**Progression:** Try to increase reps or reduce assistance weekly.

---

## **Weeks 9–11: Consolidation & Peak**

**Goals:** Maximize strength, advanced variations, peak effort.

**Warm-up:** As above, add 10 air squats and 10 scapular pull-ups.

**Main Circuit (4–5 rounds, 75s rest):**

| Exercise                | Sets x Reps         | Notes                        |
|-------------------------|---------------------|------------------------------|
| Decline Push-up (feet on chair) or regular push-up | 4–5x8–10         | Progress to decline if able |
| Pull-up (unassisted, assisted as needed, or slow negative) | 4–5x3–8          | Aim for unassisted reps     |
| Pistol Squat to chair (partial ROM) | 4–5x5/leg          | Use chair for depth control |
| Hip Thrust (shoulders on chair) | 4–5x12              | Squeeze at top              |
| Hanging Knee Raise (from pull-up bar) | 4–5x6–10          | Control swing               |

**Core/Accessory:**
- Plank with shoulder tap x10/side
- Lying leg raise x10

**Cool-down:** As above

**Progression:** Push for more unassisted pull-ups, deeper pistol squats.

---

## **Week 12: Deload & Assessment**

**Goals:** Recover, test progress, set new goals.

**Warm-up:** As above

**Main Circuit (2–3 rounds, 60s rest):**

| Exercise                | Sets x Reps         | Notes                        |
|-------------------------|---------------------|------------------------------|
| Push-up (best variation) | 2–3xAMRAP (max reps) | Test max reps                |
| Pull-up (best variation) | 2–3xAMRAP           | Test max reps                |
| Squat (best variation)   | 2–3xAMRAP           | Test max reps                |
| Glute Bridge             | 2–3xAMRAP           | Test max reps                |
| Plank                    | 2–3x max hold       | Test max time                |

**Core/Accessory:**
- Your choice, light and easy

**Cool-down:** Full body stretch

---

## **General Notes**

- **Rest:** 1 day between sessions. Light activity (walking, stretching) on off days.
- **Progression:** If client hits top of rep range with good form, progress to harder variation or add reps.
- **Form:** Prioritize quality over quantity, especially for pull-ups and push-ups.
- **Pull-up Progression:** Start with jump or negative reps, gradually reduce assistance, aim for first unassisted pull-up by week 8–10.
- **Mobility:** Encourage daily 5–10 min stretching, especially for shoulders, hips, and back.

---

## **Optional Nutrition & Recovery Tips**

- **Protein:** Aim for 1.2–1.6g/kg bodyweight daily for muscle repair.
- **Hydration:** 2–3L water/day.
- **Sleep:** 7–9 hours/night.
- **Recovery:** Foam rolling or self-massage if possible.

---

## **Summary Table**

| Phase         | Weeks | Focus                        | Key Progressions                |
|---------------|-------|-----------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Foundation    | 1–4   | Technique, base strength    | Add reps, master basics         |
| Progression   | 5–8   | Intensity, harder moves     | Reduce assistance, new exercises|
| Consolidation | 9–11  | Peak strength, advanced     | Unassisted pull-ups, pistols    |
| Deload/Test   | 12    | Recovery, assessment        | Max reps, set new goals         |

Absolutely! Here’s a beginner-friendly, sustainable nutrition plan to support your client’s 12-week strength programme. This plan is designed for a healthy 27-year-old male, aiming to build muscle and strength, with a focus on whole foods, adequate protein, and simple meal structure. Adjust portion sizes based on your client’s bodyweight, appetite, and progress.

---

## **Nutrition Plan Overview**

**Goals:**  
- Support muscle growth and recovery  
- Provide steady energy for training  
- Build healthy, sustainable eating habits

**Key Principles:**  
- Prioritize protein at every meal  
- Include plenty of vegetables and fruits  
- Choose whole grains and healthy fats  
- Stay hydrated  
- Minimize ultra-processed foods and added sugars

---

### **Step 1: Estimate Calorie Needs**

- **Maintenance Calories:** 14–16 x bodyweight in pounds (or 30–35 x bodyweight in kg)
- **Muscle Gain:** Add 200–300 kcal/day above maintenance
- **Fat Loss (if needed):** Subtract 200–300 kcal/day

*Example for 75kg male:*
- Maintenance: 75 x 33 = ~2,475 kcal/day
- For muscle gain: ~2,700–2,800 kcal/day

---

### **Step 2: Macronutrient Targets**

- **Protein:** 1.2–1.6g/kg bodyweight (90–120g for 75kg)
- **Carbohydrates:** 3–5g/kg (225–375g for 75kg)
- **Fats:** 0.8–1g/kg (60–75g for 75kg)

---

### **Step 3: Meal Structure**

**Aim for 3 main meals + 1–2 snacks daily.**  
Each meal should include:

- **Protein:** Chicken, fish, eggs, Greek yogurt, tofu, beans, lentils, lean beef, cottage cheese
- **Carbs:** Oats, rice, potatoes, whole grain bread/pasta, quinoa, fruit
- **Veggies:** At least 2 servings per meal (fresh, frozen, or cooked)
- **Healthy Fats:** Olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish

---

### **Sample Day of Eating**

**Breakfast:**  
- 3 eggs scrambled with spinach and tomatoes  
- 2 slices whole grain toast  
- 1 apple

**Snack:**  
- Greek yogurt (200g) with berries and a handful of walnuts

**Lunch:**  
- Grilled chicken breast or tofu  
- Brown rice or quinoa (1 cup cooked)  
- Steamed broccoli and carrots  
- Drizzle of olive oil

**Snack (pre- or post-workout):**  
- Banana and a protein shake (or a glass of milk)

**Dinner:**  
- Baked salmon or chickpeas  
- Roasted sweet potato  
- Mixed salad (lettuce, cucumber, peppers, olive oil)

**Optional evening snack:**  
- Cottage cheese with pineapple  
- Or hummus with carrot sticks

---

### **Hydration**

- Aim for 2–3 liters of water per day
- More if sweating heavily during workouts

---

### **Weekly Nutrition Habits**

- **Meal prep:** Batch cook proteins and grains for easy meals
- **Grocery list:** Stick to the perimeter of the store (produce, meat, dairy)
- **Limit:** Takeaways, sugary drinks, alcohol (occasional is fine)
- **Track:** Use a food diary or app for the first 2–4 weeks to build awareness

---

### **Supplements (Optional, Not Required)**

- **Whey or plant-based protein powder:** To help meet protein goals
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 3–5g/day (safe, evidence-based for strength)
- **Multivitamin:** If diet is inconsistent
- **Vitamin D:** If not getting regular sun exposure

---

### **Tips for Success**

- **Consistency beats perfection:** Aim for 80% adherence
- **Eat slowly:** Helps with fullness and digestion
- **Listen to hunger cues:** Adjust portions as needed
- **Plan ahead:** Keep healthy snacks available

---

### **Summary Table**

|-------------|--------------------|---------------------|-------------------|--------------------|
| Breakfast   | Eggs, yogurt       | Oats, toast         | Fruit, spinach    | Olive oil, nuts    |

Absolutely! Here’s how you can integrate effective, space-friendly cardio into your client’s 12-week programme. This will support heart health, recovery, and body composition, and can be done entirely at home with no extra equipment.

---

## **Cardio Plan Overview**

**Frequency:**  
- 2–3 sessions per week (on non-strength days or after strength sessions)
- Each session: 20–30 minutes

**Types:**  
- Low-impact steady-state (LISS): brisk walking in place, step-ups, shadow boxing  
- High-intensity interval training (HIIT): bodyweight circuits, jump rope (if space/ceiling allows), or short bursts of high effort

**Progression:**  
- Start with LISS in Weeks 1–4  
- Add HIIT or increase intensity in Weeks 5–12

---

## **Weeks 1–4: Foundation Cardio**

**Goal:** Build aerobic base, establish routine

**2x/week, 20–25 minutes per session**

**Options:**  
- **Marching or jogging in place:** 2–3 min  
- **Step-ups on sturdy chair/step:** 1 min  
- **Shadow boxing:** 1 min  
- **High knees (low impact):** 30 sec  
- **Rest:** 30 sec  
- **Repeat circuit 4–5 times**

**Alternative:**  
- **Dance to music** or follow a beginner YouTube cardio video

---

## **Weeks 5–8: Progression Cardio**

**Goal:** Increase intensity, introduce intervals

**2–3x/week, 25–30 minutes per session**

**HIIT Circuit Example:**  
- **Jumping jacks:** 40 sec  
- **Rest:** 20 sec  
- **Mountain climbers:** 40 sec  
- **Rest:** 20 sec  
- **Shadow boxing:** 40 sec  
- **Rest:** 20 sec  
- **Bodyweight squat jumps (or regular squats):** 40 sec  
- **Rest:** 20 sec  
- **Repeat circuit 4–5 times**

**Alternative:**  
- **Tabata:** 20 sec work, 10 sec rest, 8 rounds (4 min)  
  - E.g., burpees, high knees, fast feet, plank jacks  
- **Brisk walking in place** for 25–30 min if low impact is preferred

---

## **Weeks 9–12: Peak Cardio**

**Goal:** Maximize conditioning, variety

**3x/week, 25–30 minutes per session**

**Mixed HIIT & LISS Example:**  
- **Warm-up:** 3 min marching/jogging in place  
- **Circuit:**  
  - 1 min jump squats (or regular squats)  
  - 1 min mountain climbers  
  - 1 min shadow boxing  
  - 1 min alternating reverse lunges  
  - 1 min rest  
  - Repeat 4–5 times

**Finisher:**  
- **Burpees:** 30 sec  
- **Rest:** 30 sec  
- **Repeat 3 times**

**Optional:**  
- **Dance, follow-along cardio videos, or stair climbing** if available

---

## **General Tips**

- **Warm-up:** 3–5 min dynamic movement before cardio
- **Cool-down:** 3–5 min stretching after
- **Monitor intensity:** Aim for moderate (slightly out of breath, can talk) to vigorous (hard to talk) effort

Great question! Here’s a practical, progressive recommendation for a beginner training at home in a small flat, with a focus on versatility, space-saving, and value for money:

---

## **Best Weights to Buy for Home Strength Training**

### **1. Adjustable Dumbbells**
- **Why:** Extremely versatile, space-efficient, and allow for progressive overload as he gets stronger.
- **Recommended Range:** A set that adjusts from 2–3 kg (5–7 lbs) up to at least 20 kg (44 lbs) per dumbbell. If budget allows, sets that go up to 25–30 kg (55–66 lbs) per dumbbell are even better for long-term progress.
- **Brands:** Bowflex, PowerBlock, or budget-friendly spinlock sets.

### **2. Resistance Bands (with Handles and Loop Bands)**
- **Why:** Inexpensive, portable, and add variety for both upper and lower body. Great for rows, presses, curls, and mobility work.
- **What to Get:** A set with multiple resistance levels (light, medium, heavy).

### **3. Kettlebell (Optional)**
- **Why:** Excellent for swings, goblet squats, Turkish get-ups, and conditioning. Compact and multi-use.
- **Recommended Weight:** 12–16 kg (26–35 lbs) for most beginners; 20 kg (44 lbs) as he gets stronger.

### **4. Weighted Vest (Optional)**
- **Why:** Adds load to bodyweight exercises (push-ups, pull-ups, squats) without taking up much space.
- **Recommended Weight:** Adjustable up to 10–20 kg (22–44 lbs).

---

## **What to Buy First?**

1. **Adjustable Dumbbells** – Most versatile and useful for all major muscle groups.
2. **Resistance Bands** – Cheap, portable, and great for assistance or extra resistance.
3. **Kettlebell or Weighted Vest** – For variety and to further challenge bodyweight moves.

---

## **What to Avoid (for Small Flats):**
- Large fixed-weight dumbbell sets (take up space)
- Barbells and weight plates (unless he has a dedicated area)
- Bulky machines

---

## **Summary Table**

| Equipment           | Use Cases                        | Space Needed | Beginner Recommendation      |
|---------------------|----------------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------|
| Adjustable Dumbbells| All major lifts, isolation work  | Minimal      | 2–20 kg per dumbbell        |
| Resistance Bands    | Rows, presses, mobility, rehab   | Minimal      | Set of 3–5 bands            |
| Kettlebell          | Swings, squats, conditioning     | Minimal      | 12–16 kg to start           |
| Weighted Vest       | Loaded bodyweight exercises      | Minimal      | Up to 10–20 kg              |

---

**Start with adjustable dumbbells and bands.**  
As he progresses, add a kettlebell or weighted vest for more variety and challenge.

## **Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Intensified Strength Progression**

**Frequency:** 3 sessions/week  
**Structure:** Full-body, circuit or superset style  
**Session Length:** 40–50 minutes  
**Progression:** Increase reps, sets, and/or difficulty each week

### **General Strategies to Increase Intensity**

- **Harder exercise variations** (e.g., decline push-ups, archer push-ups, close-grip push-ups, single-leg squats)
- **Slower tempo** (e.g., 3 seconds down, 1 second up)
- **Shorter rest periods** (45–60 seconds between sets)
- **Increased sets** (from 3 to 4–5)
- **Supersets** (pairing push/pull or upper/lower moves)
- **AMRAP (as many reps as possible) finishers**

---

### **Sample Weekly Structure (Weeks 5–8)**

#### **Warm-up (all sessions, 5–7 min)**
- Cat-cow x10
- Downward dog to plank x8
- Arm circles x10/side
- Glute bridge x10
- Bodyweight squat x10
- 30s jumping jacks

---

#### **Main Circuit (4–5 rounds, 45–60s rest between rounds)**

| Exercise                        | Sets x Reps         | Notes/Progression                |
|----------------------------------|---------------------|----------------------------------|
| **Push-up Variation**            | 4–5 x 10–15         | Week 5: Regular; Week 6: Decline or close-grip; Week 7–8: Archer or tempo (3s down, 1s up) |
| **Pull-up Variation**            | 4–5 x 4–8           | Week 5: Assisted/negatives; Week 6: Add isometric holds at top; Week 7–8: Unassisted or slow negatives, AMRAP last set |
| **Bulgarian Split Squat**        | 4–5 x 10/leg        | Add 2–3s pause at bottom or slow tempo |
| **Single-leg Glute Bridge**      | 4–5 x 10/leg        | Add 2s hold at top, slow tempo   |
| **Pike Push-up or Elevated Pike Push-up** | 4–5 x 8–12   | Shoulders, progress to feet on chair if able |
| **Hollow Body Hold**             | 4–5 x 30–40s        | Add rocking or extend arms overhead for more challenge |

---

#### **Superset Example (Alternate Option)**

**A1. Push-up Variation** (see above)  
**A2. Pull-up Variation** (see above)  
*Rest 45s, repeat 4–5 times*

**B1. Bulgarian Split Squat**  
**B2. Single-leg Glute Bridge**  
*Rest 45s, repeat 4–5 times*

**C1. Pike Push-up**  
**C2. Hollow Body Hold**  
*Rest 45s, repeat 4–5 times*

---

#### **Finisher (Optional, 1–2x/week):**

- **AMRAP Push-ups:** 1 set, as many reps as possible (good form)
- **Pull-up Negative Hold:** 1 set, max time lowering from top
- **Squat Jump Tabata:** 20s on, 10s off, 4 rounds

---

#### **Core/Accessory (Rotate Each Session):**

- Side plank x30s/side
- Plank with shoulder tap x12/side
- Superman x12
- Lying leg raise x12

---

#### **Cool-down (5 min):**
- Forward fold
- Hip flexor stretch
- Chest opener
- Shoulder stretch

---

### **Progression Guidelines**

- **Week 5:** Start with regular variations, 4 rounds, 60s rest
- **Week 6:** Progress to harder variations, 4–5 rounds, 50s rest
- **Week 7:** Add tempo (3s eccentric), 5 rounds, 45s rest
- **Week 8:** Use hardest variations, AMRAP last set, 45s rest

**If he hits the top of the rep range with good form, progress to the next variation or add a round.**

---

### **Intensity Cues**

- Last 2–3 reps of each set should be challenging but doable with good form
- If a set is too easy, slow the tempo or add a pause
- If a set is too hard, regress to an easier variation or reduce reps

Absolutely! Here’s a **full-body mobility routine** your client can do 3–5 times per week, either as a warm-up, cool-down, or on rest days. It’s designed for small spaces and requires only a mat. This routine will help improve joint health, flexibility, and recovery—supporting his strength and cardio work.

## **Full-Body Mobility Routine (15–20 minutes)**

**Instructions:**  
- Move slowly and with control.  
- Breathe deeply throughout.  
- Hold each stretch/movement for 30–45 seconds or 8–10 reps per side.

---

### **1. Cat-Cow (Spinal Mobility)**
- On hands and knees, inhale as you arch your back (cow), exhale as you round your spine (cat).
- Repeat for 8–10 reps.

---

### **2. World’s Greatest Stretch (Hip, Thoracic, Hamstring)**
- Step into a deep lunge, both hands inside front foot.
- Rotate torso, reaching one arm to the ceiling.
- Return hand, straighten front leg for a hamstring stretch.
- Switch sides after 3–4 reps.

---

### **3. Downward Dog to Cobra Flow (Shoulders, Back, Hips)**
- From plank, push hips up to Downward Dog, pedal feet.
- Shift forward, lower hips, open chest into Cobra.
- Flow between positions for 6–8 reps.

---

### **4. 90/90 Hip Rotations (Hip Internal/External Rotation)**
- Sit with knees bent, feet flat, hands behind you.
- Drop knees side to side, aiming for 90° angles at each knee.
- 8–10 reps per side.

---

### **5. Lying Thoracic Rotations (T-Spine Mobility)**
- Lie on side, knees bent, arms straight in front.
- Open top arm, rotating upper back to reach behind.
- Hold, then return. 8 reps per side.

---

### **6. Shoulder Dislocates (Shoulder Mobility)**
- Use a towel or band, hold wide grip.
- Raise arms overhead and behind, then return.
- 8–10 reps.

---

### **7. Deep Squat Hold (Ankles, Hips, Back)**
- Sink into a deep squat, chest up, elbows inside knees.
- Hold for 30–60 seconds, gently rock side to side.

---

### **8. Hip Flexor Stretch (Hip Mobility)**
- Kneel, one foot forward, tuck pelvis, shift hips forward.
- Reach same-side arm overhead, lean away.
- Hold 30–45 seconds per side.

---

### **9. Child’s Pose with Side Reach (Lats, Back)**
- Kneel, sit back on heels, arms forward.
- Walk hands to one side, hold, then switch.
- Hold 30 seconds per side.

---

### **10. Neck Circles (Neck Mobility)**
- Gently circle head in both directions, 5–6 times each way.

---

|----------------------------------|------------------------------|-------------------|
| Cat-Cow                         | Spine                        | 8–10 reps         |
| World’s Greatest Stretch         | Hips, T-spine, hamstrings    | 3–4/side          |

- If short on time, pick 4–5 moves and cycle through twice.
- Focus on areas that feel tight or restricted.
- Use slow, controlled breathing to enhance relaxation and mobility.

## **Strength Training Progression**

### **Weeks 1–4: Foundation**
- **Exercises:** Incline push-ups, assisted pull-ups/negatives, bodyweight squats, glute bridges, planks, dead bugs, bird dogs
- **Sets/Reps:** 3 rounds, 8–15 reps, 60s rest
- **Focus:** Form, consistency, adding reps each week

### **Weeks 5–8: Progression (Intensity Up)**
- **Exercises:** Regular/decline/close-grip push-ups, pull-ups (negatives, isometrics, unassisted as able), Bulgarian split squats, single-leg glute bridges, pike push-ups, hollow holds
- **Sets/Reps:** 4–5 rounds, 8–15 reps, 45–60s rest, tempo/pauses, AMRAP finishers
- **Focus:** Harder variations, slower tempo, more sets, less rest

### **Weeks 9–11: Peak/Consolidation**
- **Exercises:** Decline/archer push-ups, unassisted pull-ups, pistol squats to chair, hip thrusts, hanging knee raises, advanced core
- **Sets/Reps:** 4–5 rounds, 8–12 reps, 45–75s rest, AMRAP last set
- **Focus:** Max intensity, advanced moves, peak effort

### **Week 12: Deload & Assessment**
- **Exercises:** Best variation of push-up, pull-up, squat, glute bridge, plank
- **Sets/Reps:** 2–3 rounds, AMRAP (max reps), max plank hold
- **Focus:** Test progress, active recovery, set new goals

---

## **Cardio Plan**

### **Weeks 1–4: Foundation**
- **2x/week, 20–25 min:** March/jog in place, step-ups, shadow boxing, high knees, circuit style

### **Weeks 5–8: Progression**
- **2–3x/week, 25–30 min:** HIIT circuits (jumping jacks, mountain climbers, squat jumps, shadow boxing), Tabata, or brisk walking in place

### **Weeks 9–12: Peak**
